note: Assembly-review fixes are on main (cbaa126). This board is the Nov 20 review backlog.

items.title: Constant encryption fails the run on int.MinValue or long.MinValue because Math.Abs throws.
Source string encryption rewrites literals that must stay compile-time constants (const, case labels, default parameters).
The VM tags a boxed int in an object slot as I4, so object operations throw and == compares values.
Source encryption turns interpolation holes into ToString(), so a null interpoland throws.
The UI rebuilds settings from its own fields, dropping loaded obfy.json values on Obfuscate or Save.
The incremental cache key ignores embedded dependency bytes and the signing key file.
String encryption's resource rewrite can abort on a .resources file that holds icons or images.
Resource encryption's default * pattern encrypts .resources blobs that ResourceManager cannot read. Already excluded by default and covered by tests.
The source renamer renames an extension method but not instance-style call sites.
Opaque predicates wrap out var or pattern declarations so later uses no longer compile.
The VM implements conv.u4 from a float with a signed conversion.
An unresolvable base.F() call is encoded as a virtual call and can recurse.
Enum returns are not virtualized, so the stub never unboxes a boxed integer as the enum.
ClosedSetProcessor is a singleton, so repeated runs share one NameGenerator.
Publish uses a hardcoded version and --skip-duplicate, so a release without a bump reports success and publishes nothing.
No workflow builds the MSIX or the Inno installer.
The installer build warns and then packages the original when self-obfuscation fails.
Third-party actions are pinned to floating tags in jobs that hold write and NuGet OIDC tokens.
Publish never rebuilds the native host stub, and the CI freshness check ends in exit 0.
Platform tests run weekly only, and the job can pass having run no MAUI or Blazor tests.
Tests in Category=UI run in no CI job.
Package versions are repeated in every project file with nothing enforcing agreement.
A closed-set run continues when a member assembly fails to load.
Settings load falls back to full defaults when saving a corrected value fails.
The packing AES key is the cache digest, stored as plaintext hex in the sidecar.
The packed runtimeconfig can declare a newer framework than the payload targets.
AES decrypt helpers have no length guard for input shorter than the IV.
ObfuscateBatchAsync renames each assembly independently.
The MethodEncryption base-address guard checks 0 but not -1.
Encrypted blobs are emitted byte by byte into one static constructor.
String literals with a lone surrogate are corrupted by the UTF-8 round trip.
Exceptions from called methods are rethrown with their stack trace reset.
newarr with a negative length throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException, not OverflowException.
A covariant array store throws InvalidCastException, not ArrayTypeMismatchException.
Multiple .cs inputs are renamed independently, so a shared type gets mismatched names.
The interpolated-string path ignores exclusion attributes that the plain-literal path honours.
config generate --level with an invalid value prints a stack trace.
config wizard on redirected stdin prints a stack trace.
--level is silently ignored when --config is given.
--report on a multi-file standard run covers only the first file.
Typing in an exclusion input box flips the selected preset to Custom.
A typed output directory and the symbol-map toggle are saved only at exit.
The VS Code problem matcher has no file or line group.
Visual Studio argument quoting breaks on a path ending in a backslash.
Two Visual Studio build warnings: CS8604 and a crashing analyzer (AD0001).
Project path sets use a case-insensitive comparer on Linux.
The native host build script logs "pack pkg" instead of the version on the NuGet-restore path.
The scenario harness strips the inherited Platform variable for every scenario build.
AntiDump, Watermark, and AntiDecompiler have no test that runs the output. All three now have a run.
Obfy.PackedBootstrap is missing from the coverage include list.
Scenario tests use fixed timeouts that can flake on a cold runner.
